Grupo Energia Bogota is a Colombian multinational energy group based in Bogota, active in electricity transmission, natural gas transportation and distribution (including the Cálidda network in Peru) and power generation in Colombia, Peru, Brazil and Guatemala. Customers are utilities, industrial users and households through regulated tariffs. Majority-owned by the Bogota city government and listed on the Colombian stock exchange (GEB). Roughly a century old and a regional infrastructure leader. B2B and regulated utility, low consumer brand awareness outside Colombia.

Kodiak Robotics is a Mountain View, California autonomous trucking company, founded in 2018 by ex-Google and Uber self-driving engineers, developing the Kodiak Driver for long-haul freight. Customers are trucking and logistics firms, with driverless operations in the Texas oil-field region for Atlas Energy and a long-haul network in the US Sun Belt. It went public via a SPAC merger with Ares Acquisition Corp II in 2025 (Nasdaq: KDK). B2B technology, limited consumer brand awareness.

Aadhar Housing Finance is a Mumbai-based Indian housing finance company providing home loans, mostly to low and middle-income and self-employed customers buying affordable homes, with a network of several hundred branches across India. It earns interest and fees on its loan book. Previously a Wadhwa Group firm, it was acquired by Blackstone in 2019 and listed on the Indian stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) in 2024. Sells to Indian households, moderate regional brand awareness, mostly domestic.

Alliance Laundry Systems is a Ripon, Wisconsin manufacturer of commercial laundry equipment, selling washers and dryers under the Speed Queen, UniMac, Huebsch, IPSO and Primus brands. Customers are laundromats, multi-housing laundry operators, hotels, and institutions, plus Speed Queen home laundry sold to consumers. Revenue runs in the billions of dollars with global distribution. Long owned by private equity (BDT Capital and others); it completed a US IPO in 2025 (NYSE: ALH). Speed Queen has solid consumer recognition in North America; mostly B2B overall.

Bit Origin is a New York-based crypto mining company, listed on Nasdaq (BTOG), that mines bitcoin using self-owned machines and hosted facilities in the US. It was formerly a Chinese-linked firm (previously China Xiniya, a footwear and apparel business) that pivoted to digital assets and later announced a Dogecoin treasury strategy. It earns revenue from mining rewards. Small cap, no consumer brand, little public brand awareness outside crypto investors.

Blue Owl Credit Income is a non-traded private credit fund managed by Blue Owl Capital, based in New York. It raises capital mainly from wealthy individual and retail investors and lends to mid-sized and large US companies through senior secured loans, earning interest income. Blue Owl Capital is a listed alternative asset manager (NYSE: OWL) with well over $200 billion under management. Financial product aimed at investors, little consumer brand awareness; Blue Owl is known in finance circles.

Fold is a Phoenix, Arizona fintech offering a bitcoin rewards app and Visa debit and credit cards that pay cashback in bitcoin, plus gift card and bill pay rewards. Customers are US consumers; revenue comes from card interchange and fees. It went public through a SPAC merger with FTAC Emerald in 2025 (Nasdaq: FLD) and holds bitcoin on its balance sheet. Consumer-facing crypto brand with modest awareness among US bitcoin users.

GoldState Music is described as a private investment firm focused on music assets in West Palm Beach, Florida. Industries listed are finance and financial services. The Crunchbase description says it is a private investment firm; it has reported funding of about $500 million (Feb 2026), which suggests a vehicle for acquiring music royalties or catalogs. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Paxos is a New York blockchain infrastructure company and regulated trust company founded in 2012. It issues regulated stablecoins, including Pax Dollar (USDP), PayPal's PYUSD and Global Dollar (USDG), and provides tokenization, crypto brokerage and custody infrastructure to banks, fintechs and asset managers such as PayPal, Interactive Brokers and Mastercard. Chartered by the New York Department of Financial Services. B2B infrastructure, known mainly in finance and crypto, with limited consumer awareness.

Yendo is a Dallas, Texas fintech offering consumer credit cards, notably the Yendo Card, aimed at car owners who borrow against the value of their vehicle to build credit. Customers are US consumers, many with limited credit history; it earns interest and fees. Founded by Jimmy Jones and others, it has raised significant debt and equity financing, with a reported total of about $507 million. Early-stage consumer finance brand with limited awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

GoPro is a San Mateo, California maker of action cameras (HERO series, MAX 360), mounts and accessories, plus a subscription service for cloud storage and editing. Founded in 2002 by Nick Woodman, it sells through retailers and online to consumers, adventure athletes and creators in about 100 countries. Listed on Nasdaq (GPRO) since 2014; revenue has fallen from a peak above $1.5 billion. Strong consumer brand in action sports and has a history of sports sponsorship.

Lendistry is a Los Angeles-based lender and fintech and community development financial institution (CDFI) providing loans and capital to small businesses, especially minority-owned and underserved ones, and handled large volumes of PPP loans during the pandemic. Founded in 2015 by Ken Kim and Ray Rodriguez, earning interest and fees, and acquired a bank charter via Lendistry Bank in 2024. US-focused, regional awareness among small business owners.

LMAX Group is a London-based financial technology company operating electronic trading venues, including LMAX Exchange for institutional foreign exchange, LMAX Digital for cryptocurrency trading, and FX Clearing. Founded around 2010, it serves brokers, banks, hedge funds and other institutions and earns trading, clearing and technology fees. Regulated in the UK and privately held. B2B finance brand, known in trading circles and with little consumer awareness.

meutudo is a Fortaleza, Brazil fintech whose mission is to transform credit access in Brazil. Its app serves mainly retirees, pensioners and public sector workers (INSS beneficiaries) with payroll-deductible loans, credit cards and related services. It earns interest and fees. It has raised a large amount of capital, reported at around $413 million including debt. Consumer financial brand present in Brazil only, with moderate local awareness.

Nothing is a London-based consumer electronics company founded in 2020 by Carl Pei, co-founder of OnePlus. It makes Nothing Phone smartphones, Nothing Ear and CMF by Nothing audio and wearables, known for transparent design and its Glyph light interface, and is building AI-led devices and the Essential feature in its OS. Sells directly and through retail partners in dozens of markets, mainly Europe, India and the US. It has raised about $450 million. Growing design-led consumer brand with strong youth and tech awareness.

Ratio is a San Mateo, California fintech platform that offers customers financial products. Industries given are finance and financial services. The Crunchbase description says it is a fintech platform that provides customers with financial tools; reported funding is about $424 million, mostly debt, as of April 2026. No further reliable detail is available from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Cheplapharm is a Greifswald, Germany pharmaceutical company that acquires and markets established branded prescription medicines from large pharma, such as Vistide-type legacy brands and products like Zovirax, Lariam and Xenical, selling in more than 100 countries. Customers are pharmacies, hospitals and health systems; it earns product sales revenue. Founded 1998, privately held by founder Dr Erich Kreutzer's family and investors, with large leveraged debt financing. B2B pharma, little consumer brand awareness.

Cosan is a Brazilian holding company in Sao Paulo with stakes in energy, fuel, logistics and agriculture. It holds interests in Raizen (fuel and sugar-ethanol joint venture with Shell), Rumo (rail logistics), Compass gas and Moove lubricants, which sells Mobil-licensed lubricants. Customers are industrial, retail and fuel distribution. Listed on B3 (CSAN3) and the NYSE (CSAN). Moove sponsors in motorsport in some markets, but the group mostly has B2B and local awareness.

EssilorLuxottica is a Paris-based global eyewear group formed by the 2018 merger of Essilor (lenses) and Luxottica (frames). It makes lenses and frames under Ray-Ban, Oakley, Varilux and Transitions, licenses brands such as Prada, Chanel and Armani, and retails through LensCrafters, Sunglass Hut, Pearle Vision and Target Optical. Revenue exceeds €26 billion with about 190,000 employees, operating in about 150 countries. Listed on Euronext Paris (EL), partnered with Meta on smart glasses. Very high consumer brand visibility; Oakley and Ray-Ban are major sponsors.

Hershey is a Pennsylvania-based confectionery and snack company founded in 1894, making Hershey's chocolate, Reese's, Kisses, Kit Kat (US license), Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, plus salty snacks such as SkinnyPop and Dot's Pretzels. Customers are consumers via grocery, mass retailers and convenience stores, mainly in North America, with sales of about $11 billion. Listed on NYSE (HSY), controlled by the Hershey Trust. Household-name consumer brand with heavy marketing.

JDE Peet's is an Amsterdam-based global coffee and tea company, created by the 2020 merger of Jacobs Douwe Egberts and Peet's Coffee. Brands include Douwe Egberts, Jacobs, L'OR, Tassimo, Senseo, Peet's and Pickwick, sold in more than 100 markets with revenue of roughly 9 billion euros. Customers are consumers via retailers and foodservice. Controlled by JAB Holding and listed on Euronext Amsterdam from 2020; Keurig Dr Pepper agreed to acquire it in 2025. Well-known grocery brands in Europe.

Khazna Data Centers is an Abu Dhabi-based operator of wholesale data centers, serving hyperscalers, cloud providers, enterprises and government clients in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Turkey and Italy. It is the largest data center operator in the UAE, a subsidiary of Emirati tech group e& and the AI firm G42, and has multi-gigawatt AI-focused expansion plans. Earns capacity leasing revenue. B2B infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.

Lazada Group is a Singapore-based e-commerce platform operating marketplaces in Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. Founded in 2012, it sells products from brands and sellers to consumers and earns commissions, advertising and logistics fees through its Lazada Logistics arm. Majority-owned by Alibaba since 2016-2018. Serves hundreds of millions of consumers across Southeast Asia. Very high consumer brand awareness in the region and previously sponsored sports events such as football.

Mitsui & Co is a Tokyo-based general trading company (sogo shosha), one of Japan's big five, founded 1876 and active in energy, metals, machinery, chemicals, food, healthcare and mobility. It makes money by trading, project investments and equity-accounted businesses, with operations in about 60 countries and tens of thousands of staff. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (8031). Customers are corporates and governments; B2B, brand known in business and Japan but little consumer recognition.

NBN Co is the Australian government-owned company that built and operates the National Broadband Network, based in North Sydney. It provides wholesale broadband infrastructure (fibre, fixed wireless, satellite and hybrid) to retail internet providers such as Telstra, Optus and TPG, which sell plans to households and businesses. It serves around 8.5 million premises. State-owned. The brand is well known in Australia through the retail internet connection, but it is wholesale-only.

Newell Brands (formerly Newell Rubbermaid) is a consumer goods company headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. Its portfolio includes Rubbermaid, Sharpie, Paper Mate, Graco, Coleman, Yankee Candle, Oster, Mr. Coffee, Crock-Pot, Calphalon and FoodSaver, sold mostly through mass retailers and online. Sales are about $7 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (NWL). Customers are consumers and retailers worldwide, strong household brands.

Serverfarm is a data center company based in El Segundo, California, offering a portfolio of data center infrastructure including colocation, wholesale and build-to-suit facilities, with sites in North America, Europe and Asia. It serves enterprise, cloud and technology customers and earns long-term capacity lease revenue. It has raised very large capital, reported at about $5.3 billion. Backed by institutional investors. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Shouqi Car Rental is a Beijing-based Chinese car rental and ride-hailing business, associated with the state-owned Beijing Shouqi Group (formerly Capital Automobile). It operates the Shouqi Limousine and Chauffeur brand, a premium ride-hailing service for consumers and corporate clients, and extended car rental. Last funding was in 2016. Moderate brand awareness in China, B2B and mid-market consumer. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

SK On is a South Korean electric vehicle battery maker headquartered in Seoul, a subsidiary of SK Innovation spun off in 2021. It supplies lithium-ion pouch cells and modules to Hyundai, Kia, Ford (via BlueOval SK joint venture), Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, with plants in Korea, the US, Hungary and China. A top global battery maker by market share, with debt and equity funding of over $7 billion. B2B supplier, little consumer brand awareness.

STACK Infrastructure is a Denver-based provider of wholesale data center capacity and campuses for hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises, operating in North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific. Founded in 2013 and backed by infrastructure investors including IPI Partners, it has raised more than $9 billion across equity and debt. Revenue comes from long-term capacity leases. B2B infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

Telecom Italia (TIM) is Italy's former state telephone monopoly, based in Milan. It operates fixed and mobile telecom services and ICT for consumers and businesses in Italy, and owns a major stake in the Brazilian operator TIM Brasil. In 2024 it sold its fixed network (NetCo) to KKR; the brand TIM remains. Listed on Borsa Italiana (TIT). Customers are tens of millions of mobile lines. Very high brand awareness in Italy and sponsor of football (Serie A) and cycling.

Viking Cruises is a Basel, Switzerland-based cruise line founded by Torstein Hagen in 1997, operating river and ocean cruises and expedition ships to Europe, Asia, Egypt and the Americas under Viking River, Viking Ocean and Viking Expeditions. It targets affluent older travellers, sells directly, and has fleets of over 90 ships. It listed on the NYSE in 2024 (VIK). Strong brand recognition in the US and UK, known for sponsoring Masterpiece Theatre on PBS.

Abound is a London-based UK consumer lending fintech that uses open banking data to assess borrowers' affordability and offers personal loans to people who may be turned down by mainstream lenders. Formerly Fintern/Abound, backed by firms such as Citi and Vitruvian. It raised about £1.6 billion in debt financing. Consumer finance brand in the UK with moderate awareness.

Energizer Holdings is a St. Louis, Missouri consumer goods company known for Energizer and Eveready batteries, Energizer lighting, plus automotive fragrance and appearance products (Armor All, STP, Refresh Your Car). It sells through retailers in 160-plus countries with revenue around $2.9 billion. Spun off from Edgewell in 2015, listed on NYSE (ENR). Very well-known household brand with the Energizer Bunny, a history of motorsport sponsorship.

Genting Berhad is a Kuala Lumpur-based Malaysian conglomerate under Lim Kok Thay, with leisure and hospitality (Resorts World Genting casino and theme park, Resorts World Las Vegas, Resorts World Sentosa in Singapore, Genting Malaysia), plantations, power generation and oil and gas operations. It earns revenue from gaming, hotels and cruise lines such as Resorts World Cruises. Listed on Bursa Malaysia (GENTING). Strong consumer visibility in Southeast Asia, including with gaming and entertainment brands.

Hanesbrands is a Winston-Salem, North Carolina apparel company making basics under the Hanes, Bonds, Maidenform, Playtex and Bali brands (it sold its Champion activewear brand to Authentic Brands in 2024). It sells innerwear and basics through mass retailers, wholesale and online in the Americas, Australia and Europe, with revenue of roughly $3.5 billion. Listed on NYSE (HBI); Gildan agreed to acquire it in 2025. Household brand with large consumer recognition.

Hello TransTech, formerly HelloBike, is a Shanghai-based Chinese mobility company running the Hello app, which offers shared bikes, shared e-bikes and mopeds, ride-hailing and related services, plus battery swap and EV services. Backed by Ant Group and other investors, with about $2 billion raised. Serves tens of millions of consumers in China. Widely known consumer app brand in China.

Li Auto is a Beijing-based Chinese electric vehicle maker, founded in 2015 as Chehejia and led by Li Xiang. It sells extended-range EV SUVs (L-series) and, since 2024, the battery EV Mega and i-series, alongside its own charging network. It sells through direct stores to Chinese consumers, with annual deliveries of several hundred thousand vehicles. Listed on Nasdaq (LI) and Hong Kong (2015). Strong consumer brand in China, expanding abroad.

Picnic is an Amsterdam-based online-only supermarket founded in 2015 that delivers groceries to homes using electric vans, in the Netherlands, Germany and France. It sells at near-store prices with free delivery and takes orders only through its mobile app. Investors include Edeka, Temasek and EQT, with about 1.7 billion euros raised. Serves millions of households. Strong consumer brand in the Netherlands.

Planet Fitness is a Hampton, New Hampshire franchisor of low-cost, no-intimidation gyms under the Planet Fitness name, with more than 2,700 clubs and over 20 million members in the US, Canada, Mexico, Australia and elsewhere. It earns franchise royalties, equipment sales and membership fees, with the Black Card tier. Founded in 1992 and listed on NYSE (PLNT). Consumers are mass-market members. High brand awareness in the US, a sponsor of events and television.

Qingju is a bike-sharing platform based in Chengdu, Sichuan, China, listed under electric vehicle and product industries. The input describes it as a company providing bike-sharing platforms; it reports about $2 billion in funding with the last round in February 2021. It was later associated with the Didi group's shared bike business, but the input does not confirm ownership. Consumer service in China. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Qnity Electronics is a Wilmington, Delaware company spun out from DuPont in November 2025, supplying materials and technology for semiconductor manufacturing and advanced electronics, including CMP pads and slurries, photoresists and interconnect materials. Customers are chipmakers like TSMC, Samsung and Intel and electronics manufacturers worldwide, with annual revenue near $4 billion. Listed on NYSE (Q). B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Rappi is an on-demand delivery super app founded in Bogota in 2015 and now also headquartered in Mexico City, operating in Latin America, including Colombia, Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Peru and Costa Rica. It delivers restaurant meals, groceries, pharmacy items and cash, with RappiPay credit cards and Rappi Prime subscriptions. Backed by SoftBank, Andreessen Horowitz and Sequoia with about $2.5 billion raised. Very high consumer brand awareness across Latin America, with sponsorship of football and events.

SK Horizon is a Seoul-based AI data center infrastructure company (AIDC). The Crunchbase description says it is an AI data center infrastructure company, with an unusually large reported funding figure (about 3.08 trillion Korean won, August 2026). It is likely related to the SK Group, but ownership and details are not confirmed by the input. B2B infrastructure. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Trade Republic is a Berlin-based neobroker and savings app founded in 2015, letting Europeans buy stocks, ETFs, crypto and derivatives, set up savings plans and hold a Trade Republic card, backed by a German banking licence. It serves millions of retail customers across Germany, France, Italy, Spain and other European countries. It was valued at around 5 billion euros in 2025 and earns order-flow payments, interest and card fees. Strong brand among young European consumers.

Turkcell is Turkey's largest mobile operator, headquartered in Istanbul, offering mobile, fixed broadband, TV and digital services such as BiP messaging, fizy, and Paycell, plus subsidiaries in Ukraine and Belarus. Serves roughly 40 million subscribers in Turkey. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (TCELL) and NYSE (TKC); a major shareholder is the Turkey Wealth Fund. Very high consumer brand awareness in Turkey and a sponsor of football (Turkcell Super Lig naming rights historically) and other sports.

VakifBank is a large Turkish state-controlled bank based in Istanbul, founded in 1954 and now majority-owned by the Directorate General of Foundations and the Turkey Wealth Fund. It offers retail, commercial, SME and corporate banking, insurance and asset management services via about 900 branches. It is listed on Borsa Istanbul (VAKBN) with total assets above $60 billion and serves millions of customers. High consumer brand recognition in Turkey, with a prominent sponsor of volleyball and sports.

Wistron Corporation is a Taipei-based electronics manufacturing and design company, founded in 2001 as a spin-off of Acer. It builds laptops, servers, networking and medical equipment for brands such as Dell, HP and Lenovo, plus AI servers via the Wiwynn subsidiary. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (3231) with revenue in the tens of billions of dollars. B2B contract manufacturing, little consumer brand awareness.

Wiwynn is a Taipei-based cloud computing and data center hardware company, founded in 2012 as a subsidiary of Wistron. It designs and manufactures servers, storage and rack-scale systems for hyperscale cloud providers such as Microsoft, Meta and Google, including AI servers. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (6669). B2B supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

Flex (Flex Ltd.) is a global contract electronics manufacturer and supply chain company, historically Flextronics, with operational headquarters in Austin, Texas and legal home in Singapore. It designs and manufactures products for automotive, healthcare, industrial, communications and data center clients, including power and cooling for AI data centers, with about $26 billion revenue and some 150,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (FLEX). B2B, low brand awareness among consumers.

Aditya Birla Capital is the financial services arm of India's Aditya Birla Group, based in Mumbai. It offers lending (Aditya Birla Finance), asset management (Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC), life and health insurance, housing finance and wealth management to retail and corporate customers across India. Listed on the NSE and BSE (ABCAPITAL), with a large loan book and assets under management. Strong brand in India, with the group sponsoring several sports and events.

Advanced Energy Industries is a Denver, Colorado-based maker of precision power conversion and control systems (Fort Collins origins) for semiconductor equipment, industrial thin-film, data center, telecom and medical applications. Founded in 1981, listed on Nasdaq (AEIS), with roughly $1.5 billion annual revenue. Customers are equipment manufacturers such as Applied Materials and Lam Research. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Alan is a Paris-based French digital health insurance company founded in 2016 by Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve and Charles Gorintin. It provides health insurance and healthcare services to companies and their employees, with a mobile app, and has expanded into Spain, Belgium and Canada. It holds a French insurance licence and serves hundreds of thousands of members. Raised about $1.2 billion in total with a valuation of roughly 4 billion euros. Well-known startup brand in France.

AmeriGas is a King of Prussia, Pennsylvania propane distributor, one of the largest in the US, supplying home heating, cooking, commercial, industrial and cylinder exchange customers through hundreds of branches. Now part of UGI Corporation, with the former AmeriGas Partners fully merged into UGI in 2019. Customers are residential, commercial and agricultural users across all states. Recognisable on propane cylinder exchange at retail stores; no major sports presence.

Ameriprise Financial is a Minneapolis-based financial services company, spun out of American Express in 2005. It offers financial planning, wealth management, retirement, insurance and asset management (Columbia Threadneedle Investments) through about 10,000 advisors. Assets under management and administration exceed $1.5 trillion, with an NYSE listing (AMP). Customers are affluent retail and institutional investors in the US and abroad. Strong brand recognition in the US, with sponsorship of golf and Ameriprise Invitational events.

Ant International is the Singapore-based international arm of Ant Group, created in 2023, providing digital payments, wallet and fintech services such as Alipay+, Antom, WorldFirst and Bettr. It connects merchants and users across over 100 markets, processing payments for global brands and tourism flows. Owned by Ant Group, an affiliate of Alibaba founder Jack Ma. B2B brand mostly, with the Alipay+ consumer network visible to tourists, and has sponsored sports events.

Asset World Corp is a Bangkok-based Thai hospitality and commercial property company, part of the TCC Group of billionaire Charoen Sirivadhanabhakdi. It owns and operates hotels, convention centers, retail and mixed-use developments such as Asiatique, and office buildings in Thailand and overseas. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (AWC). Customers are travellers, event organisers, shoppers and tenants. Hotel and retail brands are known in Thailand, a mix of consumer and B2B exposure.

Bajaj Finserv is a Pune-based Indian financial services holding company in the Bajaj Group, with Bajaj Finance (consumer and SME lending), Bajaj Allianz General and Life Insurance, and Bajaj Finserv Health. Listed on the NSE and BSE (BAJAJFINSV). Serves hundreds of millions of customers in India via EMI cards, loans, and insurance. Strong consumer brand in India.

Barings BDC is a Charlotte, North Carolina-based business development company externally managed by Barings, the asset manager owned by MassMutual. It is a closed-end, publicly traded fund listed on the NYSE (BBDC) that lends to middle-market private companies, earning interest income and distributing it to shareholders. Investors are institutions and retail shareholders, with a portfolio of around $2.5 billion. Financial vehicle, little consumer brand awareness.

Bell Canada, often simply Bell, is a Montreal-based telecommunications company and the largest in Canada, part of BCE Inc. (TSX/NYSE: BCE). It offers wireless, internet, TV (Fibe), landline and business network services, plus Bell Media (CTV, TSN, Crave) through its parent. It serves over 22 million subscriber connections. Very high consumer brand awareness in Canada and a major sports sponsor, including NHL, NFL broadcast rights and the Canadian Grand Prix.

Bird is the Amsterdam-based cloud communications platform formerly called MessageBird, founded in 2011 by Robert Vis. It provides APIs and software for SMS, voice, WhatsApp and email messaging, a customer-engagement inbox and a conversational AI offering, serving thousands of businesses worldwide. Revenue comes from usage and subscriptions. Backed by investors such as Accel and Y Combinator, with a peak valuation near $3 billion and about $1.5 billion raised. B2B, known among developers and marketers, little consumer awareness.

CDW is a Vernon Hills, Illinois-based provider of IT solutions, reselling hardware, software and services from vendors such as Dell, HP, Cisco and Microsoft to business, government, education and healthcare customers in the US, UK and Canada. Founded in 1984, with annual revenue above $20 billion and roughly 15,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (CDW). B2B reseller, well known to IT buyers but little consumer awareness; has sponsored sports such as NASCAR and IndyCar.

CGI is a Montreal-based global IT and business consulting firm founded in 1976 by Serge Godin and Andre Imbeau, offering systems integration, managed IT, cybersecurity and consulting to banks, governments, utilities and other large clients. It has about 90,000 employees in 40 countries and annual revenue near C$15 billion. Dual-listed on the TSX and NYSE (GIB). B2B, with limited consumer brand awareness but sponsorship in sports and culture.

Chery Holding is a Wuhu, China-based state-linked automaker, one of China's largest carmakers and top vehicle exporters, owning the Chery, Exeed, Jetour, iCar and Omoda brands and a joint venture with JLR (Freelander in China). It sells passenger cars and SUVs, including EVs, in over 100 countries. Its subsidiary Chery Automobile listed in Hong Kong in 2025 (9973). Consumer car brand with growing recognition in Europe, Latin America and emerging markets, and a football and sports sponsor.

Cloover is a Berlin-based energy-transition fintech providing embedded financial services and software for solar, storage and heat-pump installers. It offers financing, a sales platform and project management software, enabling installers to sell energy systems to households. Founded around 2021 and has raised about $1.4 billion mostly as debt facilities, with offices in Germany and elsewhere in Europe. B2B, with limited public brand awareness.

ContourGlobal is a London-headquartered power generation company, founded in 2005, that owns and operates thermal, hydro, wind and solar plants across Europe, Latin America, Africa and the US. It sells electricity mainly under long-term contracts to utilities and grids, and has been growing its clean energy share. KKR acquired it in 2022 and took it private from the London stock market. B2B energy, with little consumer brand awareness.

Cornerstone Robotics is a Hong Kong robotics company working to improve the accessibility of surgical care through surgical robot systems, such as its Sagewise soft-tissue surgical robot, aiming to make robotic surgery more affordable. Customers are hospitals and surgeons. It has raised about $1.2 billion in reported funding, mostly in recent years, and is developing its products in Asia and beyond. B2B medtech with limited public brand awareness.

D-Wave Quantum is a Palo Alto, California and Burnaby, Canada-based quantum computing company, founded in 1999, that builds annealing quantum computers (Advantage systems) and gate-model research, offered via cloud (Leap) and on-premise to enterprises, researchers and governments. Listed on the NYSE (QBTS) since going public via SPAC in 2022. Customers include Davidson Technologies, NTT Docomo and Ford Otosan. B2B deep tech with strong retail-investor interest but little brand awareness among the general public.

DeFi Development Corp (formerly Janover) is a US public company, listed on Nasdaq (DFDV), that holds Solana as its main treasury asset, running a Solana-focused digital asset treasury strategy and building related blockchain infrastructure. Previously Janover was a small commercial real estate lending marketplace. It trades on market cap and tokens rather than selling to consumers. Small cap, known in crypto investing circles, with limited consumer awareness.

eStruxture is a Montreal-based Canadian data center operator providing carrier-neutral and cloud-neutral colocation, interconnection and cloud services across data centers in Montreal, Calgary and Vancouver. Customers are enterprises, cloud platforms and network providers, who pay capacity and service fees. Reported funding is about $1.6 billion, largely infrastructure investor and debt capital. B2B infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.

Flapping Airplanes is a US artificial intelligence research lab described as a startup in AI research. The input shows reported funding of about $1.18 billion and the company is classed in artificial intelligence. No further reliable detail on its products, customers or backers can be given from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Goldman Sachs BDC is a publicly traded business development company (NYSE: GSBD) managed by Goldman Sachs Asset Management, based in New York. It lends mainly to US middle-market companies through senior secured loans, earning interest and distributing income to shareholders, with a portfolio of about $3.5 billion. Investors are institutions and retail. The Goldman Sachs name is globally recognised, though the vehicle itself is a financial product with little consumer visibility.

Great-West Lifeco is a Winnipeg-based Canadian financial services holding company that owns Canada Life, Empower (US retirement services) and Irish Life, offering life and health insurance, retirement plans, wealth management and reinsurance to millions of customers in Canada, the US and Europe. Controlled by Power Corporation of Canada and listed on the TSX (GWO). Assets under administration exceed a trillion dollars. Brand known in Canada and Europe through Canada Life and Empower, which have sponsored sports.

Groww is a Bengaluru-based Indian fintech platform, founded in 2016, offering stock broking, mutual funds, F&O trading, IPOs, loans and wealth products to retail investors. It became the largest active investor platform in India, with over 12 million active clients. Backed by Peak XV, Tiger Global, YC and others; it listed on the NSE and BSE in November 2025. Strong consumer app brand among young Indian investors, with active advertising and sponsorship.

Grupo Aeromexico is Mexico's flag-carrier airline group based in Mexico City, flying domestic and international routes to the US, Latin America, Europe and Asia from its Mexico City hub, and a founding member of the SkyTeam alliance. It carries about 25 million passengers a year, with a fleet of roughly 150 aircraft. Delta Air Lines owns a stake of around 20 percent. It returned to the Mexican exchange and the NYSE in 2025 (AEROMEX). High consumer brand awareness in Mexico.

Guidewire Software is a San Mateo, California software company, founded in 1998, providing the core platform for property and casualty insurers: policy, billing and claims systems (InsuranceSuite), plus data analytics and cloud services. Customers are insurance carriers in over 40 countries. Listed on NYSE (GWRE) with annual revenue near $1 billion. B2B enterprise software, with low consumer brand awareness.

B2B supplier with growing brand visibility, including sponsorship of UEFA football.

Electricite de France (EDF) is a Paris-based French state-owned electric utility, the world's largest nuclear power operator, generating and selling electricity and gas in France, the UK, Italy and elsewhere, with about 37 million customers and 170,000 employees. Fully nationalised by the French state in 2023. Revenue is above 100 billion euros. Very high consumer brand awareness in France, and a long-time Olympic and sports sponsor.

Enel is a Rome-based Italian multinational energy company, the largest private renewable power operator in the world, generating, distributing and selling electricity and gas in Italy, Spain, Latin America and elsewhere, with about 60 million customers. Listed on Borsa Italiana (ENEL), with the Italian government holding about 24 percent. Revenue is about 90 billion euros. Strong consumer brand in Italy, and a partner in sports including Formula E and MotoGP in the past.

Energy Transfer is a Dallas, Texas-based US midstream energy company (NYSE: ET), owning one of the largest pipeline networks for crude oil, natural gas, NGLs and refined products across the US, plus Sunoco fuel distribution. It earns fees and distribution margins from producers, refiners and utilities, with assets of about 130,000 miles of pipeline. Led by Kelcy Warren. B2B infrastructure with limited consumer exposure beyond Sunoco-branded fuel.

Groupe BPCE is a Paris-based French cooperative banking group, formed in 2009 from Banque Populaire and Caisse d'Epargne, and also owning Natixis and Credit Foncier. It serves about 36 million customers with retail banking, insurance and investment banking in France and abroad, with total assets above 1.3 trillion euros. Owned by its cooperative members. Strong brand in France, and a long-time sponsor in sports and Olympic partnership.

HDFC Bank is a Mumbai-based Indian private bank, the largest in the country by assets and market capitalisation after merging with parent HDFC Ltd in 2023. It offers retail banking, loans, cards, payments and corporate banking to more than 100 million customers through about 9,000 branches. Listed on NSE, BSE and NYSE (HDB). Very high consumer brand awareness in India, with cricket and event sponsorships.

HSBC is a London-based global bank, founded in Hong Kong and Shanghai in 1865, serving about 40 million customers in around 60 countries with retail banking, wealth, commercial banking and global markets. Total assets are about $3 trillion. Listed in London, Hong Kong and New York (HSBA, 5, HSBC). Very high global brand awareness, and a major sponsor of sports including rugby sevens and golf.

Humana is a Louisville, Kentucky-based US health insurer, listed on NYSE (HUM), best known for Medicare Advantage plans, plus Medicaid, dental, and CenterWell primary care and pharmacy services. It covers about 17 million members and has revenue above $120 billion. Customers are seniors, employers and government programmes. Strong brand among US seniors, with sponsorship in sports and the Humana Challenge golf event.

Iberdrola is a Bilbao-based Spanish electric utility and one of the world's largest renewable energy producers, with wind, solar, hydro, networks and retail in Spain, the UK (ScottishPower), the US (Avangrid) and Brazil. It serves about 40 million customers, with revenue near 45 billion euros. Listed on the Spanish exchange (IBE). Strong consumer brand in Spain and the UK, with a record of sports sponsorship including women's football and rugby.

Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) is a Beijing-based state-owned bank and the world's largest bank by assets, at over 6 trillion dollars. It offers retail, corporate and international banking through about 16,000 branches in China and more than 40 countries. Listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong (601398, 1398), majority owned by the Chinese state. Very high brand awareness in China, and a long-term Olympic and sports sponsor.

Mercuria is a Geneva, Switzerland-based commodity trading company, founded in 2004 by Marco Dunand and Daniel Jaeggi, trading crude oil, refined products, natural gas, power, metals and agricultural commodities, and investing in energy storage and renewables. One of the world's top independent trading houses with revenue above $100 billion. Privately owned by its management. B2B with low consumer awareness.

MPLX is a Findlay, Ohio-based US midstream energy partnership (NYSE: MPLX), formed by Marathon Petroleum, which owns pipelines, terminals and gathering and processing assets to move crude, refined products and natural gas liquids. It earns fees from Marathon Petroleum and third parties. Marathon Petroleum owns the majority of the units. B2B infrastructure with little consumer visibility.

National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) is an Indian government-owned development finance institution, based in Mumbai, that refinances banks for agriculture, rural infrastructure and small enterprises and supervises cooperative and rural banks. Established in 1982. Owned by the Government of India and the Reserve Bank. B2B and policy lender, with limited consumer brand awareness, though well known in rural India.

National Debt Management Center is the Saudi Arabian government's debt office, which manages and issues government debt for the Kingdom, including sukuk and bonds, and funds the government's financing programme. Based in Riyadh, it sits under the Ministry of Finance. The reported funding of about $14 billion refers to debt issuance. Government entity, no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

NextDecade is a Houston-based LNG developer, listed on Nasdaq (NEXT), building the Rio Grande LNG export facility in Brownsville, Texas, with five planned trains. Customers are utilities and energy firms like Shell, TotalEnergies, ConocoPhillips and Engie, under long-term supply contracts. It raised capital through project financing and equity of about $12 billion. B2B energy infrastructure, little consumer brand awareness.

NRG Energy is a Houston-based US power company (NYSE: NRG), generating and retailing electricity and natural gas to about 7 million homes and businesses, under brands such as Reliant, Green Mountain Energy, Direct Energy and Vivint smart home services. Revenue is about $28 billion. Customers are consumers and commercial users across the US and Canada. Reliant has recognition in Texas; NRG has sponsored sports such as the NRG Stadium naming rights in Houston.

Pattern Energy Group is a San Francisco-based renewable energy developer and owner of wind, solar, transmission and storage projects, including the SunZia Wind and Transmission project in New Mexico, with operations in the US, Canada, Mexico and Japan. Founded in 2009 and taken private by the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board in 2020. Customers are utilities and corporate offtakers. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Postal Savings Bank of China is a Beijing-based Chinese state-owned bank, with more than 40,000 outlets, the largest retail network in the country, serving over 600 million individual customers in the mostly rural and small town market. Listed in Hong Kong and Shanghai (1658, 601658) and majority owned by China Post Group. Total assets are over 16 trillion yuan. Very high consumer awareness in China.

Public Investment Fund (PIF) is the sovereign wealth fund of Saudi Arabia, based in Riyadh, with assets of over $900 billion. It invests in domestic giga-projects (NEOM, Red Sea), sports (Newcastle United, LIV Golf, Saudi Pro League clubs), gaming (Savvy Games), airlines, electric vehicles (Lucid) and aircraft leasing. Owned by the government and chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Customers are none directly; it owns many consumer brands. High profile in sport and sponsorship.

Qihoo 360 Technology is a Beijing-based Chinese internet security company founded in 2005 by Zhou Hongyi, offering antivirus software, a browser, search and mobile security, and moving to AI and enterprise security. It was taken private from the NYSE in 2016 and relisted in Shanghai in 2018 (601360). Customers are hundreds of millions of Chinese internet users, with income from advertising and services. Strong brand in China, with very little profile abroad.

QNB Group is a Doha-based Qatari bank, the largest in the Middle East and Africa by assets, owned about 50 percent by the Qatar Investment Authority and listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange (QNBK). It offers retail, corporate and wealth banking in about 28 countries, including Turkey (QNB Finansbank), Egypt and Indonesia. Strong brand in Qatar, and a sponsor of football and events such as the QNB Stars League.

Reliance Industries is a Mumbai-based Indian conglomerate, controlled by Mukesh Ambani, with businesses in oil refining and petrochemicals, retail (Reliance Retail), digital services and telecom (Jio Platforms, with over 480 million subscribers), and media and new energy. Revenue is about $100 billion with a listing on the NSE and BSE (RELIANCE). Customers are hundreds of millions of Indian consumers. Very high brand awareness in India, owner of the Mumbai Indians cricket team and a major sports sponsor.

ReNew is a Gurugram, India-based renewable energy company (Nasdaq: RNW), one of India's largest independent power producers in wind, solar, hydro and storage, with a capacity above 10 GW. It sells power to government agencies, utilities and corporates under long-term contracts. Backed by Masdar, CPPIB, Goldman Sachs and the Jain family. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Rocket Lab is a Long Beach, California launch and space systems company, founded in New Zealand in 2006 by Peter Beck, flying Electron small rockets and developing the Neutron medium-lift vehicle, and building satellites and spacecraft components. Customers include NASA, the US Space Force and commercial satellite operators. Listed on Nasdaq (RKLB) after a 2021 SPAC. B2B and government, with high profile among space enthusiasts and investors.

Rogers Communications is a Toronto-based Canadian telecom and media company, offering wireless, internet and cable to millions of customers, and owning the Toronto Blue Jays, Sportsnet, Rogers Centre and a stake in Maple Leaf Sports & Entertainment. It acquired Shaw in 2023. Listed on the TSX and NYSE (RCI). Controlled by the Rogers family. Very high consumer brand awareness in Canada and a major sports media and sponsorship player.

Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is a Toronto-based bank, the largest in Canada by market capitalisation, offering personal and commercial banking, wealth management, insurance and capital markets in Canada, the US and 25 other countries. About 98,000 employees and assets above C$2 trillion. Listed on TSX and NYSE (RY). Very high brand awareness in Canada, a long-time sponsor of golf (RBC Canadian Open, RBC Heritage), tennis and the Olympics.

Saudi Aramco is the state-owned oil and gas company of Saudi Arabia, based in Dhahran, and the world's largest producer of crude oil at around 12 million barrels a day, with refining and chemicals interests. About 82 percent owned by the government and listed on the Saudi exchange (2222). It has a major sponsorship profile, including as global partner of Formula 1 (since 2020) and title sponsor of the Aston Martin F1 team.

Shanghai Pudong Development Bank (SPD Bank) is a Shanghai-based Chinese joint-stock commercial bank, founded in 1992, offering corporate, retail and credit card services across China. Listed in Shanghai (600000), with China Mobile as its largest shareholder. Total assets exceed 9 trillion yuan. Strong domestic brand in China, with limited recognition outside it.

Sonnedix is a London-headquartered independent solar power producer, with operations across Europe, the US, Chile, Japan and South Africa, owning and operating solar plants of about 6 GW in capacity. Founded in 2009 and owned by J.P. Morgan Asset Management's infrastructure funds. It sells electricity under power purchase agreements to utilities and corporates. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

State Bank of India (SBI) is India's largest bank and a Fortune Global 500 public sector bank, based in Mumbai, with over 22,000 branches and more than 500 million customers. It offers retail, corporate, rural and international banking and owns SBI Life, SBI Cards and SBI Mutual Fund stakes. About 57 percent owned by the Government of India and listed on the NSE and BSE (SBIN). Very high brand awareness in India, and a sponsor of cricket and sports events.

Sysco is a Houston-based US foodservice distributor (NYSE: SYY), the largest in the world, delivering food, kitchen supplies and equipment to restaurants, hospitals, hotels and schools in the US, Canada and Europe, with revenue of about $80 billion and 330 distribution centers. Customers are foodservice operators, not consumers. B2B, with a recognisable truck brand but limited consumer awareness; a sponsor of golf and baseball in the US.

Talen Energy is a Houston-based independent power producer, owning nuclear (Susquehanna), natural gas and other power plants in the US PJM and ERCOT markets, and supplying data centers such as Amazon's campus. It emerged from a 2023 bankruptcy and relisted on Nasdaq (TLN) in 2024. Customers are utilities, power markets and hyperscalers. B2B energy, with no consumer brand awareness.

Targa Resources is a Houston-based US midstream energy company (NYSE: TRGP), operating natural gas gathering and processing plants, NGL pipelines, fractionators and export terminals, mostly in the Permian Basin and on the Gulf Coast. Customers are oil and gas producers and chemical firms. Revenue is around $16 billion. B2B infrastructure with little consumer brand awareness.

TenneT is an Arnhem, Netherlands-based electricity transmission system operator, wholly owned by the Dutch state, running the high-voltage grid in the Netherlands and a large part of Germany (TenneT Germany), with offshore grid connections in the North Sea. It serves about 42 million end users. Customers are utilities, generators and large industries. State-owned B2B infrastructure, with low consumer brand awareness.

TenneT Germany is the German arm of Dutch grid operator TenneT, based in Bayreuth, operating high-voltage transmission lines from Schleswig-Holstein to Bavaria, and connecting North Sea offshore wind farms. Its ownership has been partly sold to investors in 2025 (APG, GIC and Norges Bank Investment Management took a 46 percent stake). Customers are utilities, generators and industrial users. B2B infrastructure, low consumer awareness.

The Walt Disney Company is a Burbank, California-based entertainment conglomerate, founded in 1923, with studios (Disney, Pixar, Marvel, Lucasfilm, 20th Century), media networks (ABC, ESPN, National Geographic), streaming (Disney+, Hulu, ESPN+) and parks, experiences and products (Disney parks, cruise line, consumer products). Revenue is about $90 billion. Listed on NYSE (DIS). Among the most recognised consumer brands in the world, and a partner of F1 through ESPN and Star broadcast deals.

Trafigura is a Singapore and Geneva-based commodity trader, founded in 1993, trading crude oil, refined products, metals, minerals, gas, power and agricultural goods, and owning Puma Energy (retail fuel in 50 countries) and Impala Terminals. Revenue is more than $200 billion. Privately owned by employees. Customers are producers, refiners and industrials. B2B, but Puma Energy forecourts give some consumer visibility, and it has sponsored sports and arts.

TransDigm is a Cleveland, Ohio-based aerospace supplier (NYSE: TDG), owning proprietary components such as actuators, ignition systems, seating and cockpit controls for commercial and military aircraft. It grows by acquiring niche parts businesses and earns high margins on aftermarket spare parts, with revenue near $8 billion. Customers are Boeing, Airbus, airlines and the US military. B2B with no consumer brand awareness.

Uniper is a Duesseldorf, Germany-based energy company, a former E.ON spin-off, trading and generating power and gas, operating gas storage and LNG, and supplying industrial customers in Europe. It was rescued and nationalised by the German government in 2022 during the gas crisis, with the state owning about 99 percent. Revenue is tens of billions of euros. B2B energy with limited consumer awareness; planned reprivatisation by 2028.

Vistra is an Irving, Texas-based US integrated power company (NYSE: VST), generating electricity from natural gas, nuclear, coal, solar and storage, and retailing power to about 5 million customers under brands including TXU Energy, Dynegy and Ambit. Revenue is around $17 billion. Customers are homes, businesses and wholesale markets. TXU Energy is well known in Texas, and Vistra has sports stadium partnerships.

Williams is a Tulsa, Oklahoma-based US energy infrastructure company (NYSE: WMB), owning the Transco natural gas pipeline and gathering and processing assets that carry about a third of US natural gas. Revenue comes from regulated tariffs and fees paid by utilities, producers and power generators. Customers are B2B. Little consumer brand awareness, though it is well known in the energy industry.

Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank (ADCB) is a UAE bank based in Abu Dhabi, offering personal and business banking, cards, wealth and Islamic banking, listed on the Abu Dhabi exchange (ADCB) and partly owned by the Abu Dhabi government. It has assets above 500 billion dirhams. Customers are consumers, companies and government clients. Strong brand in the UAE, with sponsorship of sports and events.

ACME Solar (ACME Solar Holdings) is a Gurugram-based Indian renewable energy developer and independent power producer, listed on the NSE and BSE (ACMESOLAR) after a 2024 IPO, owning solar, wind and hybrid projects with a pipeline of several GW and offering round-the-clock renewable power. Customers are state utilities and corporates under long-term contracts. Reported funding about 391 billion rupees. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Adani Green Energy is an Ahmedabad-based Indian renewable energy company in the Adani Group, listed on the NSE and BSE (ADANIGREEN), with solar, wind and hybrid projects and a large pipeline, including the Khavda park in Gujarat. Capacity is above 15 GW. Customers are state discoms and corporates. The Adani Group has faced US indictment and short-seller allegations. B2B, with the group name widely known in India.

Adura is a UK North Sea oil and gas joint venture combining the UK assets of Equinor and Shell, formed in 2025 and based in Aberdeen. It produces oil and gas with output of roughly 140,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day. Owned 50/50 by Equinor and Shell. B2B energy, with no consumer brand awareness. The input shows reported funding of about $3 billion.

AES is an Arlington, Virginia-based global power company (NYSE: AES) that generates and distributes electricity, including renewables and storage, through utilities in the US (AES Indiana, AES Ohio) and operations in Chile, Brazil, Mexico, Panama and the Dominican Republic. Customers are utilities, industrials and households. Revenue is around $12 billion. Largely B2B with local consumer exposure, and moderate brand awareness.

Air China is a Beijing-based Chinese flag carrier, a state-owned airline of the Air China Group, operating domestic and international passenger and cargo flights from hubs at Beijing Capital and Chengdu, with about 700 aircraft, and a member of the Star Alliance. Listed in Hong Kong, Shanghai and London (753, 601111). Controlled by China National Aviation Holding. Very high brand awareness in China, and an Olympic and sports partner.

Air France-KLM is a Paris-based airline group formed in 2004 by the merger of Air France and KLM, also owning Transavia and Martinair, with about 550 aircraft carrying around 100 million passengers a year. Listed on Euronext Paris and Amsterdam (AF), with the French state holding around 28 percent. Revenue is about 31 billion euros. Very high consumer brand awareness in Europe, and a sports and cultural sponsor.

Aircastle is a Stamford, Connecticut-based aircraft leasing company that acquires, leases and sells commercial jet aircraft to airlines worldwide, with a portfolio of about 250 aircraft. It is owned by Marubeni and Mizuho Leasing. Customers are airlines. B2B, no consumer brand awareness. Reported funding in the input is about $6 billion, mainly debt.

Al Rajhi Bank is a Riyadh-based Saudi Arabian bank, the world's largest Islamic bank, offering Sharia-compliant retail, SME and corporate banking, auto and home finance, with over 500 branches and millions of customers. Listed on the Saudi exchange (1120) and founded by the Al Rajhi family. Strong consumer brand awareness in Saudi Arabia, and a sponsor of sports and events in the Kingdom.

Alabama Power Company is a Birmingham, Alabama-based regulated electric utility, a subsidiary of Southern Company (NYSE: SO), serving about 1.5 million customers across most of Alabama, with generation from nuclear, coal, gas, hydro and solar. Customers are homes and businesses. Regulated local utility, strong state brand awareness, and a sponsor of Alabama sports and universities.

Allied Irish Banks (AIB) is a Dublin-based Irish bank, rescued by the state in 2009 and now about 7 percent held by the Irish government after returning to the market, with retail, SME and corporate banking in Ireland and the UK (First Trust in Northern Ireland). Listed on Euronext Dublin and London (A5G). Customers are millions of households and businesses. Very high brand awareness in Ireland, a sponsor of GAA and other sports.

AltaGas is a Calgary, Alberta-based North American energy infrastructure company (TSX: ALA), with natural gas utilities (WGL in Washington DC, SEMCO), midstream propane export terminals and storage. It serves about 1.7 million utility customers. Revenue is around C$13 billion. Customers are households and energy firms. B2B and regulated utility, with local brand awareness through WGL.

AMC Theatres is a Leawood, Kansas-based US movie theatre chain, the largest in the world, with about 900 theatres and 9,000 screens in the US and Europe (Odeon, UCI), owned by AMC Entertainment Holdings (NYSE: AMC). Revenue is about $4.6 billion from tickets and concessions. It became a meme stock in 2021. Chinese owner Wanda was its previous controlling shareholder. Very high consumer brand awareness in the US.

American Electric Power (AEP) is a Columbus, Ohio-based US utility (Nasdaq: AEP), owning the nation's largest electricity transmission network, with generation and distribution utilities in 11 states, serving about 5.6 million customers. Revenue is around $20 billion. Customers are households, businesses and industries. Regulated utility, moderate local brand awareness, and the company has naming-rights and sports partnerships.

Apollo (Apollo Global Management) is a New York-based alternative asset manager (NYSE: APO), founded in 1990 by Leon Black, Josh Harris and Marc Rowan, with about $750 billion in assets across credit, private equity and real assets, and owner of retirement-services insurer Athene. Investors are pensions, sovereign funds and individuals. Corporate brand known in finance; it owns consumer brands through private equity investments.

Archer Aviation is a San Jose, California electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) developer (NYSE: ACHR), building the Midnight air taxi for urban air mobility, with partners United Airlines, Stellantis and the UAE launch plan in Abu Dhabi. Founded in 2018, it listed via SPAC in 2021 and has raised billions of dollars. Pre-revenue. Customers are airlines and operators. Known among investors and aviation media, with the official air taxi role at the LA 2028 Olympics.

Arevon is a Scottsdale, Arizona-based US developer, owner and operator of utility-scale solar and battery storage projects, with a portfolio of several GW. Owned by Capital Dynamics and funds, and backed by about $4.5 billion in financing. Customers are utilities and corporate buyers of power. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Athene is a West Des Moines, Iowa-based US retirement services company, now part of Apollo Global Management (merged in 2022), which sells fixed annuities and funding agreements and reinsures, with more than $300 billion in assets. Customers are retirees, institutions and employers. Previously listed on NYSE (ATH). Corporate brand known in insurance, but low general consumer awareness.

Atlas Renewable Energy is a renewable energy company focused on solar development and operation, with projects in Latin America (Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru) as well as the US, selling power to utilities and corporate buyers. The input lists reported funding of about $5.1 billion in project financing and a US base. B2B energy, with no consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Avaada is a Noida, India-based green energy company that develops solar, wind, battery storage and green hydrogen, supplying power to utilities and corporates, with a pipeline of many GW. Founded by Vineet Mittal in 2016, backed by Brookfield, Ontario Teachers and Temasek, with funding of about $6 billion. Planned an IPO of its Avaada Electro subsidiary. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Avantus is a San Francisco, California-based developer of large-scale solar and solar-plus-storage projects across the western US, formerly 8minute Solar Energy, backed by KKR. Customers are utilities and corporate buyers through long-term contracts. Reported funding about $3.5 billion. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

Aviation Capital Group is a Newport Beach, California-based aircraft leasing company, owned by Tokyo Century (Japan), with a portfolio of about 300 aircraft leased to airlines in more than 40 countries. It earns lease income. Reported funding is about $8.4 billion, mostly debt. B2B, no consumer brand awareness.

AviLease is a Riyadh-based Saudi aircraft lessor owned by the Public Investment Fund, established in 2022, which buys and leases narrow- and wide-body aircraft to airlines and has placed large Airbus and Boeing orders. The input shows about $3.7 billion in funding. B2B aircraft leasing, with no consumer brand awareness.

AXA Group is a Paris-based global insurer, founded in 1985, offering property-casualty, health, life and asset management to about 93 million customers in 50 countries, with revenue of around 100 billion euros. Listed on Euronext Paris (CS). Very high consumer brand awareness in Europe, with long-standing sports sponsorship, including rugby and golf and, in the past, football.

Axis Bank is a Mumbai-based Indian private bank, the third-largest in the country, offering retail, corporate, and wealth banking, cards and Citi India's consumer business (acquired in 2023). It has over 5,000 branches and listed on NSE and BSE (AXISBANK). Customers are tens of millions of Indians. High consumer brand awareness in India, and a sponsor of cricket and sports.

Axon is a Scottsdale, Arizona-based public safety technology company (Nasdaq: AXON), maker of TASER conducted energy devices, body cameras, Evidence.com software and drones for law enforcement and military. Revenue is about $2.1 billion, with a subscription model. Customers are police departments and governments in over 100 countries. B2B, with the TASER name widely known in public.

Aypa Power is a Houston-based US developer and owner of large-scale battery storage and renewable energy projects, backed by Blackstone Infrastructure, with several GW of capacity. Customers are utilities and grid operators. Reported funding about $4.7 billion. B2B energy, no consumer brand awareness.

Azul is a Sao Paulo-based Brazilian airline, founded in 2008 by David Neeleman, serving more than 150 destinations, mostly domestic, from its Campinas hub, with loyalty program TudoAzul. It carries about 30 million passengers a year and is listed on B3 and NYSE (AZUL). It filed for Chapter 11 in 2025. Consumers are Brazilian travellers. Strong consumer brand in Brazil, with football sponsorship.

Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena (MPS) is a Siena, Italy-based bank founded in 1472, the world's oldest surviving bank, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, wealth and insurance. The Italian state rescued it in 2017 and holds a stake; it took over Mediobanca in 2025. Listed on Borsa Italiana (BMPS). Customers are Italian households and firms. Strong brand in Italy, a sponsor of the Palio di Siena and basketball.

Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria (BBVA) is a Bilbao and Madrid-based Spanish bank with large operations in Mexico (BBVA Mexico), Turkey (Garanti BBVA), Spain and South America, serving about 80 million customers. Listed on the Madrid exchange and NYSE (BBVA). It owns the digital bank brand and has total assets above 800 billion euros. Very high consumer brand awareness in Spain and Mexico, with sports sponsorship including LaLiga and Liga MX.

Bank of Baroda is a Vadodara-based Indian public sector bank, the second-largest by assets after SBI among public lenders, founded in 1908, with about 8,000 branches in India and operations in 17 countries. About 64 percent owned by the Government of India and listed on NSE and BSE (BANKBARODA). Customers are retail and corporate. Strong brand in India, and a sponsor of cricket and sports.
